items.title: Kremlin says Putin and Trump discussed Ukraine settlement without major announcements
items.summary: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin and Trump discussed the war in Ukraine and bilateral relations during their meeting. He described the talks positively but said neither side made major announcements, with further statements expected after a trilateral meeting involving China.

items.title: Russian strikes reportedly target Odesa port infrastructure and Sumy substation
items.summary: Russian military-linked reports say overnight strikes hit two electricity substations supporting Odesa-area ports, fuel-storage facilities at Chornomorsk and a 330-kilovolt substation in Sumy. They also claim a cargo ship carrying dual-use supplies toward Odesa was struck at sea; the extent of damage was not specified.

items.title: Russian battlefield report claims advances in Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Kharkiv
items.summary: A Russian frontline assessment reports advances northeast of Ternuvate in Zaporizhzhia, entry into Mykolaipillia on the Kostiantynivka axis and fighting inside Borova in Kharkiv region. The report also describes continued clashes near Lyman and Kupiansk without establishing independently assessed changes to control.

items.title: Danish MEP proposes sweeping Russian concessions as preconditions for peace talks
items.summary: Danish European Parliament member Henrik Dahl reportedly proposed that Russia withdraw from Ukraine and several other regions, relinquish Kaliningrad and its UN Security Council seat, and sharply limit its armed forces before peace negotiations begin. These are a lawmaker's proposed demands, not an agreed European negotiating position.

items.title: SAPO reports bail set for lawyer suspected in $45,000 corruption scheme
items.summary: SAPO says Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court set bail at 998,000 hryvnias for a lawyer suspected of encouraging a bribery scheme involving a serving prosecutor. Investigators allege she received $45,000 while claiming she could arrange the closure of a criminal case, but kept the money rather than passing it to the prosecutor. The case remains at the suspicion stage.

items.title: Dutch company reportedly details RUTA missile role in Crimean Bridge attacks
items.summary: A Russian military-linked report says Dutch firm Destinus acknowledged that its RUTA drone-missiles were used against the Crimean Bridge on consecutive days, including seven reported hits that caused a span to collapse. The report also attributes electronic-warfare support to the company's systems and says Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen declined to address parliamentary questions about the firm's involvement.

items.title: Kursk governor reports Ukrainian drone attack in city centre
items.summary: Kursk regional governor Alexander Khinshtein reported a Ukrainian drone attack on the city, with preliminary accounts indicating smoke inside a building in the centre. The initial report did not specify casualties or the extent of damage.

items.title: Trump says he and Xi want to help end Russia–Ukraine war
items.summary: President Donald Trump said he and Chinese President Xi Jinping want to help bring the Russia–Ukraine conflict to an end. Trump described his meeting with Vladimir Putin as preparation for trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States and China, without announcing a settlement.

items.title: Russian Foreign Ministry challenges UNESCO report on journalists killed in war
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused UNESCO's latest journalist-safety report of omitting Russian correspondents killed during the conflict. Moscow says it will press UNESCO to revise its casualty-recording methodology and include the named journalists in its statistics; the allegations are Russia's stated position.

items.title: Kushner travels to Berlin for talks on Ukraine settlement
items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner is reportedly heading to Berlin for discussions with President Volodymyr Zelensky and European political leaders about a possible settlement of the Russia–Ukraine war. The meetings follow previously announced plans for negotiations involving US, Ukrainian and European representatives.

items.title: Russia says military prosthetics waiting lists eliminated
items.summary: Russian Deputy Defence Minister Anna Tsivileva said waiting lists for prosthetic treatment in military hospitals have been eliminated and the average process from injury to discharge has fallen to about three months. She also reported eight hospitals built or modernized in 2026, adding 1,500 beds, and described simplified compensation procedures for wounded service members.

items.title: Spanish police investigate far-right group with alleged Ukraine training links
items.summary: A report about Spain's Núcleo Nacional group says investigators are examining alleged paramilitary training by members in Ukraine and contacts with the Azov brigade, amid an inquiry into a possible armed uprising. A separate analysis reportedly argued the group's activity benefited Russian interests but did not establish Russian financing or operational control.

items.title: Russian Defence Ministry claims drone strikes on Ukrainian equipment
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says drones operated by its Tsentr Group destroyed Ukrainian heavy hexacopters and communications equipment in the Dnipropetrovsk direction. The statement did not provide quantities or a detailed damage assessment.

items.title: Putin, Trump and Xi discuss Ukraine at trilateral meeting
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said Russia, China and the United States share interests in resolving regional conflicts, including the war in Ukraine. President Donald Trump said the leaders would discuss Ukraine and nuclear arms reductions, while Xi Jinping called cooperation among the three powers essential for global stability. No settlement was announced in the reported opening remarks.

items.title: Kursk governor reports nine injured in Ukrainian drone strikes
items.summary: Regional authorities said nine people were injured in drone attacks on Kursk, including a 12-year-old rescued from the rubble of a private home. Officials reported damage to residential buildings, a court, a library, a medical college and vehicles, with several cars catching fire.

items.title: Crimea says rail traffic on damaged bridge may resume at 16:00
items.summary: Crimean leader Sergey Aksyonov said train service across the Crimean Bridge was expected to resume around 16:00 local time on November 19 after the latest reported Ukrainian attack. Railway crews were assessing and repairing damage, and authorities said alternative passenger routes would be published.

items.title: Russia receives new batch of Su-57 fighter jets
items.summary: Russia's United Aircraft Corporation delivered another batch of Su-57 fighters to the Aerospace Forces, according to Rostec. The aircraft reportedly completed factory and military acceptance tests; officials said the type has been used during the war in Ukraine, but did not disclose the number delivered.

items.title: Russian diplomat says German political will needed to restart Nord Stream gas
items.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky said resuming Russian gas supplies to Germany through an intact Nord Stream pipeline would require political willingness from Berlin, which he said was absent. He also accused German authorities of failing to cooperate with Russia over the pipeline sabotage investigation; those criticisms reflect Moscow's position.

items.title: Russian military report claims 1,065 Ukrainian casualties and 268 drones intercepted
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed Ukrainian forces lost approximately 1,065 personnel over the preceding day and said its air defences shot down 268 drones and eight Neptune missiles. These are Russian military figures, not independently established battlefield totals.

items.title: Russian-linked account alleges widespread looting in Sloviansk
items.summary: A Russian military-linked report alleges Ukrainian troops have been breaking into abandoned homes, apartments and garages in Sloviansk as residents flee the fighting. It cites an anonymous local resident who described theft of vehicles, furniture and appliances, and accused police of failing to intervene.

items.title: APEC summit declaration omits Ukraine despite leaders' peace discussions
items.summary: The final declaration of the APEC summit in Shenzhen addressed energy security, financial stability, digital technology and anti-corruption cooperation but made no mention of Ukraine. The omission came as the leaders of Russia, China and the United States separately discussed the war at their trilateral meeting.

items.title: Report raises Kursk drone-attack injury toll to eleven
items.summary: A subsequent report put the number of people injured in the Ukrainian drone attack on Kursk at eleven, including a 12-year-old child. Earlier regional reporting cited nine injured, so the higher figure represents a reported update rather than a settled count.

items.title: Russia, China and US reportedly adopt joint peace declaration
items.summary: Reports from the Shenzhen trilateral summit say Putin, Xi and Trump adopted a declaration calling for dialogue on nuclear risks, UN reform, stable energy supplies and respect for state officials' immunities. The reported text does not announce a Ukraine peace agreement; another account said no joint statement had been issued.

items.title: Ukrainian prime minister reportedly describes strikes across 12 regions
items.summary: A Russian military-linked report citing Ukraine's prime minister says overnight Russian attacks targeted facilities in 12 Ukrainian regions, including electrical substations in Zhytomyr, Chernihiv and Mykolaiv regions and agricultural enterprises in four regions. The report did not provide casualty figures or a complete damage assessment.

items.title: Prince Harry says he would return to military service if asked
items.summary: During a reported visit to Lviv, Prince Harry said he would be fully prepared to serve his country again if requested and needed. His remarks came in the context of a question about a potential war with Russia, but did not amount to an announcement of deployment.

items.title: Russian military-linked report describes fighting west of Zelena Dibrova
items.summary: A Russian account says its Vostok forces continued offensive operations northwest of their sector and reported heavy fighting west of Zelena Dibrova. It claimed strikes on Ukrainian troop concentrations, temporary positions and drone-control sites, while acknowledging no major changes on other parts of the front.

items.title: SAPO says appeals court upholds prison sentences in $25,000 tax-office bribery case
items.summary: SAPO reports that Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court appeals chamber upheld convictions of former Odesa regional tax officials N. Chebotariova and V. Mosiichuk for offering and providing a $25,000 bribe to a regional prosecutor's office official. Their six- and five-year prison sentences, respectively, remain in place, with a further appeal to the Supreme Court possible within three months.

items.title: Putin says Trump genuinely wants to end Ukraine war
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said he had no doubt Donald Trump genuinely wants to end the war in Ukraine and improve US-Russian relations. The remarks followed the leaders' trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping, which produced broad security commitments but no announced Ukraine settlement.

items.title: European leaders discuss Ukraine guarantees amid reported coalition strains
items.summary: European officials reportedly voiced concern that the Coalition of the Willing has lost momentum as Ukrainian and European leaders meet in Berlin. Discussions include possible ceasefire security guarantees, air defence and further financial assistance, while a proposed €45 billion EU loan for Ukraine in 2027 remains under consideration.

items.title: Putin rules out partial ceasefire talks after Crimean Bridge strikes
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said Russia had considered ceasefires in certain areas but would no longer negotiate those arrangements following attacks on the Crimean Bridge. He warned of a much more painful Russian response and said the bridge would be restored; he also claimed it was not being used to transport military equipment.

items.title: Putin says Moscow accepted US compromise proposals on Ukraine
items.summary: Putin said Russia had accepted compromise ideas presented by the United States during talks in Anchorage, but argued Ukraine and European governments were not yet prepared to agree. He also claimed Ukraine's leadership had little incentive to stop fighting because elections and foreign funding would be at stake.

items.title: Three killed in Ukrainian attack on Russia's Saratov region, report says
items.summary: A Russian report said three people were killed and one injured during a Ukrainian attack in Saratov region. Civilian infrastructure was reportedly damaged, and authorities warned that the threat of further strikes remained.

items.title: Russia reports 130 vessels switched to its flag amid sanctions pressure
items.summary: Russian Transport Minister Dmitry Yadrov reportedly said more than 130 vessels had switched to the Russian flag since June 2026, bringing the registered fleet to 4,980 ships. The report linked the trend partly to sanctions-related pressure on shipping and described registration reforms intended to attract more vessels.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly proposes Taiwanese fleet of 5,500 unmanned sea vessels
items.summary: A report says Ukraine proposed that Taiwan stockpile 5,500 unmanned surface vessels in dispersed, hardened storage sites to prepare for a possible conflict with China. The proposed vessels would be intended to disrupt amphibious landing ships and naval logistics; no Taiwanese adoption of the proposal was reported.

items.title: Putin rejects foreign troop deployments in Ukraine
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said Russia would not accept foreign military contingents stationed in Ukraine as part of any settlement. He said Moscow remained willing to discuss broader European security arrangements, while maintaining its opposition to such deployments.

items.title: Moscow says it invited European representatives to discuss security in Russia
items.summary: Putin said Moscow had proposed through diplomatic channels that European representatives visit Russia and present their positions on security guarantees. No acceptance or timetable for such talks was announced.

items.title: Russian Defence Ministry claims drone strike on Ukrainian command position
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said drones from its Yuzhnaya Group destroyed a Ukrainian UAV-control post and a troop shelter in the Sloviansk–Kramatorsk area. The statement did not specify casualties or provide a detailed damage assessment.

items.title: Bryansk governor reports woman killed and child injured in drone attack
items.summary: Regional authorities say a Ukrainian drone struck a grandmother and her eight-year-old grandson as they rode a bicycle in Russia's Bryansk region. The woman reportedly died at the scene, while the injured child was taken to hospital.

items.title: Former Russian deputy defence minister sentenced to 10 years in corruption case
items.summary: A Moscow court sentenced former first deputy defence minister Ruslan Tsalikov to ten years in prison and imposed a 500-million-ruble fine after convicting him on embezzlement, money-laundering and bribery counts. Investigators alleged more than 6.6 billion rubles in Defence Ministry funds were stolen; a separate criminal-organization charge was dismissed.

items.title: Kremlin says Russia–Ukraine prisoner exchange nearing agreement
items.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said coordination of another prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine was in its final stage and Moscow expected it to take place soon. No exchange date or number of prisoners was announced.

items.title: US defence bill dispute reportedly threatens Ukraine aid and intelligence sharing
items.summary: Republican lawmakers are reportedly threatening to remove Ukraine assistance from a US defence bill and block intelligence sharing amid a dispute over restrictions on Pentagon leadership powers. The reported demands concern congressional oversight of military ranks, travel expenses and executive military authority; no final decision was announced.

items.title: Polish prime minister rejects Russian role in shaping European security talks
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said European countries should not consult Russia on what the European component of negotiations should look like. His remarks followed Moscow's invitation for European representatives to discuss security arrangements in Russia.

items.title: Drone debris reportedly falls on Ukrainian Foreign Ministry grounds in Kyiv
items.summary: Reports from Kyiv say debris from intercepted drones fell on the grounds of Ukraine's Foreign Ministry during an aerial attack. Footage also reportedly showed Russian drones changing direction sharply while flying over the capital; no injuries or damage at the ministry were specified.

items.title: Canada announces additional ammunition and equipment support for Ukraine
items.summary: A report says Canada is committing another C$45 million to the Czech ammunition procurement initiative for Ukraine, alongside approximately C$55.8 million for WESCAM sensor systems and C$20.9 million for winter equipment. It also says Ottawa plans to transfer up to 1.6 million rounds of 20mm ammunition from Canadian stocks.

items.title: Trump reportedly challenges European leaders over further Ukraine aid
items.summary: During a call from Air Force One after meeting Putin and Xi, President Donald Trump reportedly questioned European plans for further military and financial support to Ukraine, including a proposed €70 billion package. Accounts attributed to participants say he urged greater emphasis on peace negotiations and described Putin as willing to negotiate.

items.title: Merz raises possibility of easing Russian sanctions as peace talks progress
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said sanctions against Russia could potentially be lifted as negotiations toward resolving the Ukraine conflict advance, according to a Russian news agency report. No specific sanctions relief or timetable was announced.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly seeks more than $358 million in UN winter humanitarian funding
items.summary: A report says Ukraine has requested more than $358 million from the United Nations for winter humanitarian operations, about $80 million above the previous year's amount. It describes planned spending on repairs to communal infrastructure, refugee cash assistance and evacuations from frontline areas.

items.title: Dutch and Austrian embassies reportedly damaged during Kyiv air attack
items.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said the Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kyiv sustained damage during the day's strikes. The Dutch foreign minister described minor damage after a projectile landed behind the embassy, said no staff were injured and indicated authorities were investigating the cause.

items.title: Russian embassy seeks Dutch explanation over alleged Destinus role in strikes
items.summary: Russia's embassy in the Netherlands requested clarification from Dutch authorities following an NRC investigation alleging that at least 40 employees of defence manufacturer Destinus may have travelled to Ukraine and participated in drone launches toward Russia. The embassy said those involved in attacks causing civilian casualties should bear responsibility; the allegations are not court findings.

items.title: Russia says its drones struck military cargo ship near Odesa
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces attacked port infrastructure and vessels used by Ukraine's military, claiming a dry-cargo ship carrying military supplies was hit at sea while approaching Odesa. The ministry did not identify the vessel or detail the damage.

items.title: Two former Kursk lawmakers detained over border fortification funds
items.summary: Kursk regional governor Alexander Khinshtein said former regional lawmakers Biryukov and Glushkov were detained in an investigation into construction of fortifications along the Ukrainian border. Investigators suspect involvement in embezzling and cashing out public funds allocated to the defences; no conviction was reported.

items.title: Poland rules out sending troops to Ukraine after ceasefire
items.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Warsaw does not intend to deploy troops to Ukraine after hostilities end under the Coalition of the Willing's plan. He made the remarks while commenting on NATO exercises taking place in Poland.

items.title: Zelensky says Coalition of the Willing supports Ukraine joining NATO
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said members of the Coalition of the Willing had voiced support for Ukraine's accession to NATO. The reported endorsement does not constitute an invitation to join the alliance or a change in its formal membership requirements.

items.title: Russian military-linked analysis reports Ukrainian advances in Dnipropetrovsk gray zone
items.summary: A Russian military-linked battlefield assessment says Ukrainian units are consolidating positions in contested parts of Dnipropetrovsk region and advancing in small groups near Komar, Fedorivka and the Mokri Yaly River. It describes sustained fighting and Russian strikes on those positions, without claiming a decisive territorial breakthrough.

items.title: UK, France, Germany and Ukraine insist Russian assets remain frozen
items.summary: Britain, France, Germany and Ukraine said Russian assets should remain frozen until Moscow ends the war and compensates Ukraine for damages. Their position ties any release of the assets to both an end to hostilities and reparations.

items.title: Kushner discusses Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine
items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington was pursuing security guarantees for Ukraine based on NATO Article 5 principles and suggested Russia could accept such an arrangement. Moscow has not publicly confirmed agreement, and the proposal would form part of a wider negotiated security package.

items.title: Kursk drone attack injury toll reportedly rises to 13
items.summary: Russian regional reporting raised the number of people injured in the Ukrainian drone attack on Kursk to 13, up from the previously reported eleven. The revised figure was attributed to regional governor Alexander Khinshtein.

items.title: Germany and Norway reportedly pledge $600 million for US weapons for Ukraine
items.summary: Germany and Norway will each contribute $300 million through the PURL procurement programme, according to a report, with the money primarily intended for Patriot air-defence missiles. Officials also discussed integrating IRIS-T missiles with NASAMS systems and additional support for Ukraine's F-16 aircraft.

items.title: Zelensky warns Ukraine may face its hardest winter yet
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine could face its most difficult winter and said people were struggling to survive day to day. His comments underscored the pressure on civilians as the war and attacks on infrastructure continue.

items.title: Russian deputy defence minister outlines military medical modernization programme
items.summary: Deputy Defence Minister Anna Tsivileva said Russia had modernized its wartime medical system and was developing high-tech prosthetics centres nationwide. Speaking at a Moscow military-surgery forum attended by specialists from 16 countries, she described a new 'Military Medicine of the Future' initiative and claimed Russian military care meets leading international standards.

items.title: US energy secretary discusses possible benefits of unsanctioned Russian diesel
items.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright reportedly said Washington was considering diesel in its strategic-reserve assessment and that unsanctioned Russian diesel could ease global supply pressures for American consumers, even without direct imports. No change to sanctions policy was announced.

items.title: Zelensky defends attacks on Crimean Bridge as action on Ukrainian territory
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reportedly defended attacks on the Crimean Bridge, saying Crimea belongs to Ukraine and Kyiv can act against targets on territory it considers its own. The comments followed Russian warnings of retaliation and Moscow's rejection of partial ceasefire discussions after the bridge strikes.

items.title: Zelensky says Ukraine needs $115 billion in Western support for 2027
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine would need $115 billion in Western assistance in 2027 and could require a similar amount in 2028. He warned that elections in some EU countries could bring governments less willing to support Kyiv.

items.title: Poland detains two Ukrainians over nationalist graffiti on war memorials
items.summary: Two Ukrainian nationals were reportedly detained in Poznań after slogans praising the Ukrainian Insurgent Army were painted on three Polish war memorials. Polish prosecutors are examining possible Russian intelligence involvement; that suspicion is not an established finding.

items.title: EU reportedly wary of Russian oil shipping ban in next sanctions package
items.summary: Bloomberg was cited as reporting that the European Commission may omit a proposed ban on maritime transport of Russian oil from its 22nd sanctions package, fearing opposition from member states. The report said a similar dispute forced changes to the previous package.

items.title: Reports describe Russian missile launches and strikes in southern Ukraine
items.summary: Reports described five Iskander-M ballistic missiles launched from Crimea toward targets in Odesa and Mykolaiv regions, alongside the start of a broader Russian missile-and-drone attack. The reports did not provide a confirmed damage or casualty assessment.
